GO DOWNSTAIRS.

questions.title: Cut and color your hair
questions.situation: You are Kara, at the bathroom mirror upstairs in the squat, with the scissors. You are going to cut your hair short so that nobody looking for a runaway android will know you. What color will it be?

options.text: BROWN: cut it short and keep it brown.
BLACK: cut it short and dye it black.
WHITE: cut it short and dye it white.
BLONDE: cut it short and dye it blonde.

questions.title: Across the street
questions.situation: You are Connor, with Lieutenant Hank outside the convenience store where the runaway AX400 was seen last night, across the street from a row of abandoned houses. Hank lets the bus driver go: “Alright, that’s all for now. Free to go.” Officer Ben: “We’ve got officers sweeping the neighborhood, in case anybody saw anything.” Hank: “Okay. Well, let me know if they turn anything up.” Ben: “What are you gonna do with that?” Hank: “I’ve no idea…”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Ralph’s meal
questions.situation: You are Kara. Downstairs, Ralph is back. He is leaping around Alice with a knife and a dead animal, a large rodent, and she is terrified. Ralph: “Ralph found this to feed the little girl… It’s good for her… A present… To make up for past misunderstandings… Ralph’ll cook… We will do just like humans do. Humans like burnt meat… Come! Come and sit down!”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: “Come and sit down!”
questions.situation: You are Kara, with Alice and Ralph by the fire. Ralph wants you both to sit down at his table.

options.text: SIT: sit down at the table with Alice.
REFUSE: thank him, but say you have to go.

questions.title: “We will eat together”
questions.situation: You are Kara. Ralph will not let you leave until Alice has eaten. He still has the knife.

options.text: SIT: sit down at the table with Alice.
REFUSE: tell him you are leaving now, and take Alice’s hand.

questions.title: At Ralph’s table
questions.situation: You are Kara, at Ralph’s table with Alice. Ralph is cooking the animal on the fire, knife in hand.

options.text: [CHECK GUN]: feel for the gun under your clothes.
WORRIED: ask him not to hurt her; you are friends.
EXPLAIN: tell him humans don’t eat that.
AGREE: say you will eat together, like a family.

questions.title: “What did she say?”
questions.situation: You are Kara, at the table. Ralph: “That’s better. Ralph went to a lot of trouble to find something for the little girl to eat. It wouldn’t be polite for her to refuse, would it? Great. It’s going to be great. Succulent you’ll see. Succulent. Succulent. Father, mother, little girl.” Alice whispers to you: “Please, Kara. I don’t wanna eat that!” Ralph: “What did she say?”

options.text: LIE: tell him she can’t wait to eat it.
TRUTH: tell him she doesn’t want to eat it.

questions.title: “Go ahead, eat.”
questions.situation: You are Kara, at the table with Alice. Ralph puts the burnt meat in front of her: “Go ahead, eat. EAT! Eat.” He still has the knife; there is another on the table.

options.text: [ASK ABOUT CORPSE]: tell him you saw the body upstairs.
[INSIST ABOUT CORPSE]: tell him there is no point in lying; he is a murderer.
THREATEN: grab the knife from the table and tell Ralph to get back.
BLUFF: tell him you are going to stand up and leave.
FAMILY: remind him that a father would never threaten his little girl with a knife.

questions.title: Still at the table
questions.situation: You are Kara, still at the table with Alice and Ralph. He has not let you go.

options.text: [ASK ABOUT CORPSE]: tell him you saw the body upstairs.
[INSIST ABOUT CORPSE]: tell him there is no point in lying; he is a murderer.
THREATEN: grab the knife from the table and tell Ralph to get back.
BLUFF: tell him you are going to stand up and leave.
FAMILY: remind him that a father would never threaten his little girl with a knife.

questions.title: Still at the table
questions.situation: You are Kara, still at the table with Alice and Ralph. He has not let you go.

options.text: [ASK ABOUT CORPSE]: tell him you saw the body upstairs.
[INSIST ABOUT CORPSE]: tell him there is no point in lying; he is a murderer.
THREATEN: grab the knife from the table and tell Ralph to get back.
BLUFF: tell him you are going to stand up and leave.
FAMILY: remind him that a father would never threaten his little girl with a knife.

questions.title: “Anybody home?”
questions.situation: You are Kara. A voice at the front door: “Anybody home?”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The squat
questions.situation: You are Connor. There is blue blood on the fence around one of the abandoned houses: another android has been here. You knock at the door, walk round to the front and go in. Hank waits outside. Inside, a scarred android in old clothes meets you, twitching and muttering to himself.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Interrogate the squat android
questions.situation: You are Connor, inside the squat, facing the scarred android. What do you ask him?

options.text: AX400: ask whether he has seen an AX400.
DEVIANTS: ask whether there are any other androids here.
REASSURE: tell him not to be afraid; you are not going to hurt him.
BLUE BLOOD: tell him there is blue blood on the fence, and another android was here.
PRESSURIZE: tell him you know he has seen it.

questions.title: Investigate the ground floor
questions.situation: You are Connor, on the ground floor of the squat. Ralph, the scarred android, keeps close to you; his stress rises and falls as you move about. There is a table, a fire burning in the fireplace, a door to the kitchen, and the stairs, with an old arcade machine beside them. Hank is waiting outside. You do one thing at a time, in any order.

options.text: CHECK UPSTAIRS: go up the stairs and ask whether anyone is up there.
ANALYZE SQUAT ANDROID: scan him.
CHECK TABLE.
CHECK UNDER THE STAIRS: go round the side of the stairs, by the arcade machine.
CHECK KITCHEN: look through the kitchen door.
CHECK FIREPLACE.
LEAVE THE SQUAT: go back out to Hank.

questions.title: Under the stairs
questions.situation: You are Connor. As you step round the side of the stairs, Ralph throws himself on you and holds you back: “RUN! QUICK! KARA!” The AX400 and the girl burst out from their hiding place under the stairs and run for it. Hank, from outside: “Connor, what’s going on?” You: “It’s here! Call it in!”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The squat android is gone
questions.situation: You are Connor, leaving the squat with Hank. You look back into the room: the scarred android is gone. It looks as if you were alone in there.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Undiscovered
questions.situation: You are Kara, hidden under the stairs with Alice. You hear the police leave. You crawl out. Ralph is back. You: “Thanks.” Ralph: “Protect the little girl… The humans must not find her.”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The pursuit
questions.situation: You are Connor. The AX400 and the girl are on the run, and officers are after them. You: “Which way did it go?” An officer: “That way - they’re headed for the train station!”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Run toward their last known position
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the streets near the train station. Officers are running after the AX400 and the girl; one waves you toward an alley. Beyond it a fence separates the streets from a busy highway. Hank is somewhere behind you.

options.text: Run after them as fast as you can, over every obstacle.
Follow the officer into the alley, and go no further.
Stay where you are and leave the chase to the officers.

questions.title: Lost
questions.situation: You are Connor. The officers come back without them. You: “We lost it.” Hank: “Game over, Connor.”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Too late
questions.situation: You are Connor, at the fence above the highway, too late. On the far side of the traffic the AX400 and the girl have made it across, and they are gone.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: At the highway
questions.situation: You are Kara. You and Alice have climbed down a fence onto the edge of a highway: lanes of cars and trucks at full speed, a narrow middle section, and more lanes beyond. The android who has been chasing you is at the fence behind you, with police. Someone shouts: “Don’t shoot! We need it alive!”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The first lanes
questions.situation: You are Kara, at the edge of the highway with Alice. The android chasing you is at the fence behind you. The only way is across, through the traffic.

options.text: Run across the first lanes with Alice, between the cars.

questions.title: Hank’s order
questions.situation: You are Connor, at the fence above the highway. The AX400 and the girl have reached the middle section. Hank catches up: “Oh fuck, that’s insane…” You start to climb the fence. Hank: “Hey! Where you goin’?” You: “I can’t let them get away.” Hank: “They won’t! They’ll never make it to the other side.” You: “I can’t take that chance.” Hank grabs your shoulder: “Hey, you will get yourself killed! Do NOT go after ’em, Connor, that’s an order!”

options.text: GIVE UP: stay behind the fence, as Hank orders.
GO: climb over and go after them across the highway.

questions.title: The last lanes
questions.situation: You are Kara, with Alice in the middle section of the highway. The android has stayed behind the fence. More lanes of traffic lie between you and the other side.

options.text: Cross the last lanes with Alice.

questions.title: Into the traffic
questions.situation: You are Connor, on the highway, with cars and trucks bearing down on you. The AX400 and the girl are in the middle section ahead.

options.text: Cross the first lanes to the middle section.

questions.title: Caught
questions.situation: You are Kara, in the last lanes of the highway with Alice. The android has caught up and has hold of you, with cars racing past on both sides.

options.text: Fight free of him.

questions.title: The car
questions.situation: You are Connor, thrown off by the AX400 and down in the last lanes of the highway. A car is coming straight at you.

options.text: Get out of its way.

questions.title: The last lanes
questions.situation: You are Kara, with Alice in the middle section of the highway. Behind you, a car has just hit the android who was chasing you. More lanes of traffic lie between you and the other side.

options.text: Cross the last lanes with Alice.

questions.title: The other side
questions.situation: You are Kara. You and Alice reach the far side of the highway. Behind you, across the traffic, the android who chased you is still on his feet. You kneel beside Alice: “Are you okay?”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The other side
questions.situation: You are Kara. You and Alice reach the far side of the highway. Behind you, the android who chased you lies on the road where the car hit him. You kneel beside Alice: “Are you okay?”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: On the highway
questions.situation: You are Connor. On the highway, a car has hit the AX400 and the girl. Neither of them gets up. Hank: “Argh, Jesus Christ!..” He is badly shaken.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Ferndale Station
questions.situation: You are Markus, standing among the human passengers of a crowded train in the afternoon. Since the landfill you have worn a coat taken from a human and no longer have the light at your temple, so nobody gives you a second look. Overhead, the announcements play: “Customers are reminded that all androids must ride in the designated area.” “We are now approaching Ferndale Station.” “Please take care when stepping onto the platform.” The doors open and you step out. A memory plays back on its own: the landfill in the rain, and the broken android who caught hold of you there. “There’s a place where we can be free! Find Jericho! Find Jericho!..” When he touched you, he left something in your memory that you could not read at the time.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The red mural
questions.situation: You are Markus, on the platform. A man walks past on his phone: “Hey. Yeah, I’m good. How about you? … I know! It’s crazy, right? Sure, I’ll talk to you later.” A homeless man stops you: “Hey, mister, can you spare some change?..” Two passengers are talking: “I heard that android boyband is going to win some music prize.” “God, they are so creepy.” “My kids don’t listen to anything else.” To your left as you came off the train, a large red mural covers the wall: a figure with a halo and, on its chest inside a red circle, a small mark, a square with an arrowhead above and below it and a bar on either side. Nobody else on the platform looks at it twice. You scan the mark, and the key in your memory decodes it: it is a sign left for androids, and it shows you what the next sign looks like.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: A magazine on the bench
questions.situation: You are Markus, on the platform at Ferndale Station, before the escalators down to the street. Someone has left a digital magazine on a bench; you can swipe from one cover story to the next.

options.text: Read Detroit Today: Android on the Run!.
Read Tech Addict: CyberLife’s ‘Fortune Teller’ Computer.
Read Tech Addict: Android Astronauts to Explore Io.
Take the time to go through all of it.
Move on without looking.

questions.title: At the foot of the escalators
questions.situation: You are Markus. You ride the escalator down toward the street exit. At the bottom a man hurrying round the corner bumps into you: “Oh, sorry… excuse me…” On a bench a girl asks her mother: “Are we really going to get rid of Mandy?” “Grandma says it leaves her with nothing to do, sweetie.” “But she’s so cool!” “I know, honey.” Outside, to the left, an android stands waiting in a marked bay at the bus stop. Straight ahead, a mural of a lion and a boxer covers a wall: the next sign of the trail.

options.text: Ask the android at the bus stop the way to Jericho.
Leave the android be and follow the signs.

questions.title: Following the signs
questions.situation: You are Markus, following the trail through the streets. The lion-and-boxer mural holds two marks; you scan both, and the preview leads you on. Across the street, past two crosswalks, a building wall is painted with a colorful rainbow, and two more marks are hidden in it. A homeless man calls to the passers-by: “I need a dollar, I haven’t eaten all day! … Spare some change?” Children are playing nearby: “Tag! You’re it!” “I’m gonna catch you!” You keep to the left sidewalk down to where the street ends at a fence. Behind it, on a wall, is a mural of a robot. Through the fence you can scan two of its marks; the third is hidden behind a wooden plank leaning against the wall.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The junkyard
questions.situation: You are Markus. Once you have scanned the two marks you can see, you crouch and crawl under the fence, stand, and move the wooden plank away from the wall. The robot mural’s third mark was behind it; you scan it. The streets are behind you now: you come out into a junkyard of wrecked cars and scrap. On the wall to the left is a large white mural of a head, the next sign. To the left of where you came in, a white car blocks your view of the corner behind it.

options.text: Look behind the white car to the left of where you came in.
Go straight to the white mural.

questions.title: The dumpster
questions.situation: You are Markus, at the white mural of a head. From the ground you can scan only one of its marks; the others are out of sight from here. A dumpster stands nearby. You pull it over to the wall beside the mural, climb onto it and pull yourself up onto the roof.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Across the gap
questions.situation: You are Markus, on the roof. From up here you can see the white mural’s other two marks: a black one on the far left of the head, and a white one on its forehead just above the eye, almost invisible against the white paint. You scan both. Across the roof, the building ends at a gap over a drop, and the trail goes on beyond it. You preconstruct the way across, running each move in your mind before you make it, then take it: a run, a kick off the wall, and you land on the far side and drop down into the next yard.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The yard
questions.situation: You are Markus, in a yard of containers below a tall brick building. High on its wall is a faded red advertisement for spark plugs, and the preview tells you the next sign is in it. A climbing route leads up the building toward a door. The far left side of the yard, by a container, is still unexplored.

options.text: Look around the far left side of the yard, by the container.
Go straight to the building.

questions.title: The abandoned office
questions.situation: You are Markus, below the tall building. You scan the three marks in the faded advertisement. Then you preconstruct a way up: keep to the left wall, jump for the ladder, pull yourself up. You climb it the way you saw it, reach the door at the top and go in. Inside is an abandoned office, dim and empty, with pillars across the room and a broken wall at one side.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The office
questions.situation: You are Markus, in the abandoned office. The preview of the last sign matches no single surface: part of it is painted on a pillar and part on the wall behind, and it will only come together from the right spot. Straight ahead of the door, a pillar hides part of the room from view.

options.text: Look behind the pillar straight ahead.
Look for the spot where the last sign comes together.

questions.title: The ship
questions.situation: You are Markus, moving around the office until a pillar lines up with the wall behind it and the two halves of the last mark become one. You scan it. It points you to the rubble behind the broken wall at the side of the room. You climb through and come out into the open, above the old docks. Below lies a huge, rusted freighter, its blue hull lettered in big white capitals: JERICHO.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The docks
questions.situation: You are Markus, on the docks by the ship. Straight ahead, an old rusted bridge leads out toward it. At the end of the area, past a metal railing and a stairway, a crane stands over the ship with its arm reaching out above the hull.

options.text: Walk out onto the bridge straight ahead.
Head for the crane at the end of the area.

questions.title: The crane
questions.situation: You are Markus. You climb the metal railing at the end of the area, go up the stairs and climb the ladder onto the crane. You walk out along its arm to the very end, high above the ship, with dark water below. You jump.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Inside the boat
questions.situation: You are Markus, surfacing in water inside the ship. It is almost completely dark. You pull yourself up a ladder to a heavy door and work its handle slowly until it opens. In a metal case on the wall beyond, you find a flashlight and take it. Its beam shows a long corridor lined with yellow hatches; the ones that open lead only to empty rooms, and the rest are locked. At the end of the corridor you get under some rubble and open the yellow hatch on the left. It leads into the machine room.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The people of Jericho
questions.situation: You are Markus, in the machine room. You go down the metal stairs and out across a catwalk. It collapses under you and you fall. When you look up, you are not alone: androids stand around you in the dark, staring at you. One of them steps forward. “Welcome to Jericho.”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Lunch break
questions.situation: You are Connor. It is November 6th, 2038, early afternoon. You get out of the car and follow Lieutenant Hank to a food truck on a street corner, where he eats most days. Hank: “Whoa! Hey! Hey! Hey!” The owner, Gary: “Hank. How’ you doing?” Hank: “Eh, you know, same old shit.” Gary, looking at you: “Plastic with you?” Hank: “Only temporary…” A man at the serving hatch, Pedro: “Hey, hey, hey... Hank! How you doin’, man?” Hank: “¡Ese!” Pedro: “Hey, listen, I got a shit-hot tip for you. Number five in the third, Lickety-split! That filly’s one hell of a chaser. You wanna flutter?” Hank: “Last shit-hot tip you gave me set me back a week’s wages, Pedro…” Pedro: “Come on, this is different, it’s 100% guaranteed. You can’t go wrong.” Hank: “Yeah, right… Alright, I’m in.” Pedro: “Damn straight! Hey! You won’t regret this!” Your objective reads RECONCILE WITH LT. HANK.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Hank insults Connor
questions.situation: You are Connor: the replacement sent after the body that was hit by a truck on the freeway this morning, carrying its memory. You find Lieutenant Hank at the food truck where he eats lunch. The owner, Gary, hands him his food: “Here you go.” “Yeah, thanks.” “Hank. How’ you doing?” “Uh, you know, same old shit.” “Usual.” “Yeah.” Then Hank sees you: “What the fuck?..” You: “Sorry, Lieutenant. It took me a while to find you.” Hank: “Are you gonna come back like this every time you get killed?” You: “My predecessor was unfortunately destroyed, but CyberLife transferred its memory and sent me to replace it. This incident should not affect the investigation.” Hank: “Not affect the investigation? I just saw you get... hit by a truck! Now you come back like if nothing happened!” You: “A machine was destroyed. And another machine was sent to replace it. I don’t understand what’s bothering you.” Hank: “Okay, fuck you. Fuck you!”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The food truck
questions.situation: You are Connor, at the food truck while Hank waits for his order. Your scan can analyze the people and things around you, one at a time; when you are done, step up to Hank.

options.text: Scan Pedro, the man who sold Hank the tip.
Scan Hank.
Scan Gary, the owner, inside the truck.
Scan the food hygiene license at the upper left of the serving hatch.
Step up to the serving hatch beside Hank.

questions.title: Hank turns on you
questions.situation: You are Connor, at the serving hatch beside Hank. He turns on you: “What is your problem? Don’t you ever do as you’re told? Look, you don’t have to follow me around like a poodle!”

options.text: APOLOGIZE FOR BEHAVIOR: say you are sorry for how you behaved at the police station.
PARTNERS: say that now you are partners, you should get to know each other.
RECONCILE: suggest you forget what happened and start over.
REVIEW FACTS: suggest reviewing what you know about deviants.

questions.title: Hank’s lunch
questions.situation: You are Connor. Gary hands Hank his order: “Here you go.” Hank: “Ah! Thanks, Gary. I’m starving…” Gary, nodding at you: “Don’t leave that thing here!” Hank: “Huh, not a chance! Follows me everywhere… See…” He carries his burger and an enormous soda to one of the tables nearby. You can scan his meal before you join him.

options.text: Scan Hank’s drink.
Scan Hank’s hamburger.
Join Hank at his table.

questions.title: At Hank’s table
questions.situation: You are Connor, standing at Hank’s table while he eats. What do you say?

options.text: [GAMBLING]: ask about the bet Pedro offered him.
[CHOLESTEROL]: warn him about what is in his meal.
[COMPANY]: warn him that his friends are engaged in illegal activities.
HABIT: ask whether he eats here often.
FREE MEAL: point out that he did not pay for his meal.
ENJOY YOUR MEAL: wish him a good meal.
AREA: remark that he seems to know everyone in the district.
Say nothing more and get down to business.

questions.title: Down to business
questions.situation: You are Connor, at Hank’s table. The small talk is over; you turn to the case.

options.text: [HIGHWAY]: ask why he did not want you to cross the highway this morning.
ABOUT CONNOR: ask whether there is anything he would like to know about you.
HANK AND ANDROIDS: ask why he hates androids so much.
DEVIANTS: offer to tell him what you know about deviants.

questions.title: Have you dealt with deviants?
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank, between bites: “You ever dealt with deviants before?” You answer: “A few months back… A deviant was threatening to jump off the roof with a little girl… I managed to save her…”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Have you dealt with deviants?
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank, between bites: “You ever dealt with deviants before?”

options.text: TRUTH: tell him about the girl on the roof, and that you failed.
LIE: say this is the first time.

questions.title: Done your homework?
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank: “So, I guess you’ve done all your homework, right? Know everything there is to know about me?”

options.text: TRUTH: tell him what his file says.
LIE: say you are focused on the case and the rest does not concern you.

questions.title: Your conclusion
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank puts down his burger: “So, what’s your conclusion?”

options.text: SINCERE: say working with an officer with personal issues is a challenge you are built for.
PSYCHOLOGICAL: say you would like to earn his trust and solve the case together.
COLD: say you are focused on the case, not here to make judgements.

questions.title: In the elevator
questions.situation: You are Connor. At the food truck you told Hank: “I just got a report of a suspected deviant. It’s a few blocks away. We should go have a look. I’ll let you finish your meal. I’ll be in the car, if you need me.” Now you stand in the elevator of a run-down building with your eyes closed. Hank, from the corridor: “Hey Connor! You ran outta batteries or what?” You: “I’m sorry, I was making a report to CyberLife.” Hank: “Uh... Well, do you plan on staying in the elevator?” “No! I’m coming.” Hank: “What do we know about this guy?” You: “Not much. Just that a neighbor reported that he heard strange noises coming from this floor. Nobody’s supposed to be living here, but the neighbor said he saw a man hiding a LED under his cap.” Hank: “Oh Christ, if we have to investigate every time someone hears a strange noise, we’re gonna need more cops. Hey, were you really makin’ a report back there in the elevator? Just by closing your eyes?” “Correct.” “Shit... Wish I could do that…”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The corridor
questions.situation: You are Connor, walking down the corridor behind Hank toward the apartment the neighbor reported. Halfway along, on the right, there are feathers on the floor.

options.text: Examine the feathers.
Walk on to the door.

questions.title: Into the nest
questions.situation: You are Connor, at the apartment door with Hank. You knock. No answer. You knock again: “Anybody home? Open up! Detroit Police!” There is a noise inside. Hank: “Stay behind me.” “Got it.” He kicks the door in. The apartment is dark, filthy and full of pigeons. Hank: “What the fuck is this?! Jesus, this place stinks… Uh, looks like we came for nothin’, our man’s gone…”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Magazines in the first room
questions.situation: You are Connor, just inside the apartment. In the first room to the right of the door, before the room with the birds, two magazines lie on a table. Reading takes time, and Hank will not wait long.

options.text: Read Detroit Today: Red Ice Epidemic.
Read Green Earth: Past the Tipping Point.
Take the time to go through all of it.
Move on without looking.

questions.title: Investigate the apartment
questions.situation: You are Connor, searching the apartment with Hank, among the pigeons. In the main room: a poster on the wall, a military jacket, a driver’s license, a bird cage lying on the floor, a chair, a pack of birdseed, a refrigerator and a closet. In the bathroom: the sink, and a wall covered in writing above an overturned stool. Each thing you examine takes time, and Hank is in no mood to stay. What do you do?

options.text: Examine the urban farm poster on the wall of the main room.
Pull the poster off the wall.
Examine the military jacket.
Examine the driver’s license.
Examine the sink in the bathroom.
Look at the writing that covers the bathroom wall.
Examine the overturned stool under the writing.
Reconstruct what happened at the stool.
Examine the bird cage on the floor of the main room.
Reconstruct how the cage came down.
Go to the chair under the ceiling and look up.
Examine the pack of birdseed.
Open the refrigerator.
Open the closet.
STAY: ask for a couple more minutes.
LEAVE: go with him.

questions.title: Hank and Connor leave the apartment
questions.situation: You are Connor, following Hank out of the apartment and down the corridor. The suspect was never found.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The deviant drops from the ceiling
questions.situation: You are Connor. You step to the chair and look up. A man in a cap drops out of the ceiling past you in a storm of pigeons and bolts out of the apartment. Hank, flailing at the birds: “God damn fuckin’ pigeons! What are you waiting for?! Chase it!” Your objective: CATCH THE DEVIANT.

options.text: Run after him: out of the door, along the corridor and onto the roofs.
Stay where you are.

questions.title: Over the rooftops
questions.situation: You are Connor, chasing the deviant across the rooftops toward the urban farm. Your scan previews two routes.

options.text: EASY BUT SLOW: take the higher route around the roofs.
FAST BUT RISKY: jump the gap to the next roof, straight after him.

questions.title: The wheat fields
questions.situation: You are Connor, dropping down onto the wheat fields of the rooftop farm. The deviant is running between the crops. Your scan previews three routes.

options.text: SAFER DETOUR: go round by the storage depot.
FAST BUT RISKY: cut straight down through the lower wheat field.
BALANCED: run along the higher wheat field.

questions.title: The terraces
questions.situation: You are Connor, running across the farm’s terraces after the deviant. Workers look up as you pass. Your scan previews three routes.

options.text: SAFER DETOUR: go through the flower garden.
DIRECT BUT CROWDED: run along the terrace, through the workers.
DIRECT BUT SLOW: go straight through the hydroponics racks.

questions.title: The greenhouses
questions.situation: You are Connor, closing on the deviant among the greenhouses. A small farm train runs below. Your scan previews two routes.

options.text: SAFER DETOUR: go through the greenhouse.
FAST BUT RISKY: run over the greenhouse roof, through the window and onto the moving train.

questions.title: The last stretch
questions.situation: You are Connor, almost on the deviant. Your scan previews two routes.

options.text: SAFE BUT SLOW: go round the construction area.
DIRECT BUT CROWDED: go straight through the corn field and the workers.

questions.title: The deviant pushes Hank
questions.situation: You are Connor, gaining on the deviant across a rooftop of the farm. Hank has taken a separate route and gets to him first: “STOP RIGHT THERE!” The deviant shoves him. Hank goes over the edge of the roof and catches it with his hands; he is hanging there, several stories up. The deviant runs on.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Hank on the ledge
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank is hanging from the edge of the roof by his hands. Your analysis: CHANCE OF SURVIVAL: 89%. The deviant is getting away across the roofs. You have only a moment.

options.text: CHASE DEVIANT: leave Hank and go after the deviant.
SAVE HANK: pull Hank back up.
Press neither: hesitate until the moment passes.

questions.title: Inside Jericho
questions.situation: November 6th, 2038, 5:13 pm. You are Markus. You have found Jericho: the dark hold of an old ship, where androids who ran from their owners hide. Some huddle by fires; many are damaged. You are wounded in the abdomen and losing blue blood. Three androids stand in front of you, and one of them has just said: “Welcome to Jericho.” You ask: “Who are you?” “Fugitives… just like you... My name is Josh.” “I’m Simon.” A young woman: “North.”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Who they are
questions.situation: You are Markus, in the hold of Jericho with Josh, Simon and North, who have just told you their names. What do you say to them?

options.text: TRAIL: say that they knew only an android could follow the trail.
ANDROID: ask how many of them there are.
JERICHO: ask whether this is Jericho.
REFUGE: say you thought Jericho was a place where androids lived in freedom.
FREE?: ask whether hiding just to stay alive is their idea of freedom.

questions.title: More freedom than you ever had
questions.situation: You are Markus, in the hold of Jericho. Josh: “I understand how you feel... but we have more freedom here than you ever did.” How do you answer?

options.text: LOST: say you came looking for hope and will not find any here.
SOMBER: say that maybe you were never really free, and now need to decide who you are.
LUCID: say that fear has only become their new master.
DIRECT: say that waiting in the dark is not how you see freedom.

questions.title: The hold
questions.situation: You are Markus, free to walk around the hold of Jericho. Your objectives: settle in, and explore Jericho. Damaged androids sit or stand in the gloom. Josh is by the wall, watching over a small boy android. North sits on a box, bouncing a ball against a wall. A damaged android sits on the floor. Crates are stacked by the wall. Simon stands in the middle of the room. You can do one thing at a time, in any order; once you have seen Lucy and explored the hold, you can go to Simon.

options.text: Go over to the female android standing near the fire at the side of the hold.
Go over to Josh and the boy he is watching over.
Go over to North and talk to her.
Talk to the damaged android sitting on the floor.
Light the four oil drums in the hold.
Go and see Lucy, behind the white plastic sheet.
Check the crates by the wall.
Go to Simon in the middle of the room.

questions.title: North
questions.situation: You are Markus, with North in the hold of Jericho. She sits on a box and keeps bouncing a ball against the wall. What do you ask her?

options.text: TIME HERE?: ask how long she has been here.
WOUNDED: say that a lot of the androids here are in bad shape.
JERICHO: ask who found this place.
YOU: ask what her function was before she came here.
SPARE PARTS: ask why nobody has gone to get spare parts and blue blood.

questions.title: Markus hatched a plan
questions.situation: You are Markus, in the middle of the hold of Jericho. “Simon! I know where we can find spare parts... The CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor, they have everything we need.” Simon: “The docks are guarded. We can’t just walk in there and take what we want... Humans will never let us…” “Which is why we won’t ask permission.” Josh: “We don’t have any weapons… and even if we did, none of us knows how to fight.” “We can steal what we need without fighting.” Josh: “We’ll just get ourselves killed.” “Maybe, but it’s better than waiting here to be shut down.” North: “I’m with you.” Simon, looking at Josh: “Maybe it’s worth a try...” Josh: “Ok… I’m in.”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Zlatko’s house
questions.situation: You are Kara. It is evening. You and Alice have crossed the city to a lonely old house, the address an android on the street gave you. “You gonna be okay? We’ll get some help here. Soon, this will all be just a bad memory. This is the place…” The man who opens the door looks you over. “Are you Zlatko?” “Who’s asking?” “I was told you could help us…” “I don’t know who told you that. You came to the wrong place. I’m sorry.” “Wait! We really need your help…” He lets you in after all: “Come in. Come on in, don’t be shy! Luther, would you be so kind as to take these ladies’ coats? Oh, don’t be afraid of our big friend here. Luther is just another android that I helped. He keeps me company in this big, empty, old house… Please, make yourselves at home. How did you hear about me?” “An android… on the street, he said you could help us…” “I see… Deviant, huh?.. What about her?” “She’s human.” “And... You wanna find a safe place. Somewhere where you can start a new life. I hear Canada is very lovely at this time of year. Beautiful landscapes, open spaces, clean air... and no android laws! Great place for a fresh start...” “Yes, that’s… that’s exactly what we want…” “Of course! I can help you. But first we have to get rid of your tracker. All androids are fitted with a tracking device to locate them at all times. I’ll remove yours and then you’ll both be safe. Come on, follow me. Ah, the little one can wait for us in the living room.” “No, she always stays with me.” “Of course. Right this way… Everything we need is in the basement…”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Alice has a bad feeling
questions.situation: You are Kara. On the way to the basement stairs, Alice holds you back and whispers: “I don’t like this place, and that man. Let’s go, I have a bad feeling…”

options.text: CAREFUL: agree with her, and tell her you have to be careful.
REASSURE: tell her it will be okay; he will remove your tracker and you can start over in Canada.
COMFORT: admit he is a bit odd, but say you think you can trust him.
NO CHOICE: tell her you have nowhere else to go.

questions.title: The basement
questions.situation: You are Kara. Zlatko leads you and Alice down to the basement, along a corridor lined with cell doors. Odd noises come from behind one of them, and Alice stops in front of it. “Come on, Alice.” In a laboratory full of machines, Zlatko: “Please, excuse the mess… I needed somewhere discreet for my machines… Removing trackers is illegal, so I opted for discretion over comfort… I hope the little one isn’t too scared…” “No… No, she’ll be all right…” “That’s good… If you could just stand over there.” You step into the machine, and restraints close on your arms. Zlatko: “I should warn you, this could be quite unpleasant... You know what’s strange? For some unknown reason, the trackers seem to stop working in deviants... That’s why it’s so hard to find them... So, actually there’s no reason to remove your tracker...” “What? But you said that-” “Yeah, people believe what they want. You deviants are so naive. They all come to me, expecting me to help them. And I just reset them, sell them on. Or I keep them for my little experiments...” “No! No! I don’t wanna be reset! Let me go!” Alice: “KARA!” Zlatko: “I forgot about the… child... Um, lock it up, I’ll deal with it later.” Luther carries Alice away. “ALICE! ALICE! NO!” Zlatko: “Wow! A deviant that wants to be a mother… That’s... that’s so sweet! And so deluded… I think it’s time we put you outta your misery. That’s what you get for having a dream… It always ends up the same way… Tears and disillusionment… Believe me, you’re better off being erased and feeling nothing… No more pain… No more hopes dashed… I almost envy you.” On the screens: PREPARING MEMORY WIPE.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The machine
questions.situation: You are Kara, strapped into Zlatko’s machine in the basement. On the screens: MEMORY WIPE PROGRESS. Alice is gone. Your arms are held, but you can still move a little: a small red cart stands within reach beside a lamp, and two cables hang overhead, a green one above a bottle of vodka. When the wipe completes, you will remember nothing.

options.text: Fight it: shove the red cart into the lamp, pull the green cable down onto the vodka bottle and tear yourself free.
Do nothing and let the procedure run.

questions.title: Your new master
questions.situation: You are Kara, though you no longer know it. REINITIALIZATION PROGRESS: the bar fills and you open your eyes. You are a household android, and your master is Zlatko. He drags in a little girl. Zlatko: “Oh, poor little Alice. Aw! Looks like Mommy doesn’t remember you at all, huh? Looks like Mommy’s completely forgotten you!” The girl: “Kara! Kara, what happened to you?” Zlatko: “Alright, that’s enough, come on.” She bites him. “You bit me! I’m gonna teach you some manners, you little bitch…” As he pulls her away: “Kara! Wake up, Kara!” The big android, Luther, turns to you: “Meet me in the living room.”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Serving Zlatko
questions.situation: You are Zlatko’s servant. In the living room Luther hands you a tray: “Master’s dinner’s ready. Take it up to him.” “Yes, Luther.” You carry it upstairs to Zlatko’s workshop. Zlatko, at his bench: “Uh, just set it down on the table over there. Get rid of that carcass. Uh, take it next door. Did you hear what I said?” “Yes, Zlatko.” He calls out: “Luther! Luther!” “Yes, Zlatko.” “I should be done here in ten minutes or so. I’ll have a look at the little one, see what I can do with her.” “Understood, Zlatko. I’ll bring you the little one in 10 minutes.” You carry the android torso into the storage room next door and lay it on a table. In the corner of the storage room, a polar bear android paces in a cage. Nobody gives you another order.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The cells
questions.situation: You are Kara, free of the machine. Alice is gone: Luther carried her off on Zlatko’s order. In the basement corridor, behind the cell door Alice stopped at on the way in, something moves. A voice: “Help us…” Through the bars you see androids twisted into strange shapes.

options.text: Open the cells.
Leave them and go upstairs to find Alice.

questions.title: Upstairs
questions.situation: You are Kara. You climb up from the basement and slip through the house. From upstairs, Zlatko’s voice: “Luther! Luther!” “Yes, Zlatko.” “I should be done here in ten minutes or so. I’ll have a look at the little one, see what I can do with her.” “Understood, Zlatko. I’ll bring you the little one in 10 minutes.” In the upstairs hallway Luther stands waiting. He sees you, and does not call out: “I… I’m sorry… about the little one…”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: In Zlatko’s house
questions.situation: You are Kara, in Zlatko’s house. Luther said he would bring the little one to Zlatko in ten minutes; the clock is running. Each thing you do takes about a minute. Upstairs, off one corridor, are Zlatko’s workshop, a storage room, a bathroom, a bedroom, a big room with a fireplace and a TV, and a locked door at the far end. On the ground floor are the entrance hall and the living room; below them is the basement with its cells.

options.text: Open the locked door at the end of the upstairs corridor.
Look through the hole in the locked door at the end of the upstairs corridor.
Look at the book lying on a chair by the fireplace in the big room.
Look into the fire in the big room’s fireplace.
Look at the fireplace in the big room.
Switch on the TV in the corner of the big room.
Read the magazine on the bedroom nightstand: “Arctic Tensions Escalate”.
Read the magazine on the bedroom nightstand: “How Androids Alter Your Brain”.
Read the magazine on the bedroom nightstand: “AX400 Getaway”.
Pick up the shotgun on the bedroom nightstand.
Go into the bathroom.
SHUT DOWN: switch the android in the bathtub off.
ALICE: ask him whether he has seen a little girl.
DEAL: ask him whether he will keep quiet if you let go.
SPARE: tell him you will not hurt him.
Go into the storage room.
Open the cage of the polar bear android in the storage room.
Look at the pipe on the shelf between the two doors of the storage room.
Look at the corner of the storage room where you carried the torso in.
Look at the marks scratched into the wall in the corner of the storage room, by the workshop door.
Look at the living-room table where you picked up the tray.
Look at the coat rack in the entrance hall.
Look in the mirror by the stairs down to the basement.
Go down to the basement and look into the cells.
Open the cells in the basement corridor.
Wait where you are.

questions.title: Luther goes to collect Alice
questions.situation: You are Kara. You lead Alice out of the little room and along the corridor into the big room. Behind you, Zlatko: “Luther!” “Yes, Zlatko.” “I’m finished here. Go fetch the little one.” “Right away, Zlatko.” A moment later: “Zlatko! The little one is gone!” “Well, it can’t have just disappeared. It’s gotta be here somewhere! What are you waiting for? Go look!”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The big room
questions.situation: You are Kara, in the big room with Alice: a table in the middle, a closet on each side, the fireplace with its glowing embers, and two doors, the left one to the bedroom. Zlatko, somewhere close: “Luther! What the fuck are you doing? Come here!” Luther: “Coming!” Heavy steps are coming toward the room.

options.text: Hide with Alice under the table in the middle of the room.
Hide with Alice in one of the closets.
Slip through the left door into the bedroom now.
SET FIRE: take a burning ember from the fireplace and set the house alight.

questions.title: The big room, after Luther
questions.situation: You are Kara, hiding in the big room with Alice. Luther has gone. You whisper to her: “They’re searching the house... We’ve got to get out before they find us.” The left door leads to the bedroom; the embers still glow in the fireplace.

options.text: Go through the left door into the bedroom.
SET FIRE: take a burning ember from the fireplace and set the house alight.

questions.title: The bedroom
questions.situation: You are Kara, in Zlatko’s bedroom with Alice: a bed, a closet, a nightstand, and a door to the corridor. Footsteps: Zlatko is coming in. “Shit… Where are they? Luther! Find them for fuck’s sake!”

options.text: Hide under the bed with Alice.
Hide in the closet with Alice.

questions.title: The corridor
questions.situation: You are Kara, in the upstairs corridor with Alice. Zlatko and Luther are moving through the rooms behind you. The bathroom door is right beside you; at the far end of the corridor are the stairs down.

options.text: Slip into the bathroom, quickly.
Keep going along the corridor to the stairs.

questions.title: The android in the bathtub
questions.situation: You are Kara, in the bathroom with Alice. The android in the bathtub sees you.

options.text: Silence him for good.
Spare him and get out of the bathroom.

questions.title: The storage room
questions.situation: You are Kara, in the storage room with Alice, crouched behind a shelf. You whisper: “We can’t stop now. We just need to be brave, Alice…” Zlatko and Luther come in and walk between the shelves. In the corner, the polar bear android paces in its cage; tables and shelves stand between you and the far door.

options.text: Make for the bear’s cage and open it.
Stay behind the shelves and wait for a gap in their patrol.

questions.title: Zlatko closes in
questions.situation: You are Kara, hiding with Alice behind the last table by the storage-room door. Zlatko has a flashlight and is closing in: “I know you’re there, you sneaky bitch… Show yourself. Get a flashlight. There’s one on the table. Come on, show yourself… Look, I’m not gonna hurt you… I only wanna talk with you… I know I shouldn’t have erased your memory, ok? I regret that now… Now just, come on out and everything will be all right, I’ll help you… Think about that little girl. How… how scared she must be… Just be reasonable. Come out and everything will be all right…”

options.text: RUN OUT: make a run for the door with Alice.
PUSH AWAY: shove Zlatko aside.
THROW: throw something at Zlatko.
Stay hidden.

questions.title: The yard
questions.situation: You are Kara. You and Alice run down the stairs; the front door is locked, so you go out by the back door. Rain. “Hurry, Alice! Hurry! Don’t look back! Run!” Alice falls. Zlatko catches up, shotgun raised. “ALICE! GO, ALICE!” Alice: “No, I won’t leave you!” “GO! RUN AS FAST AS YOU CAN!” Zlatko: “I warned you! Dreams always end in tears… You should’ve listened to me… What are you doing? Get outta my way!” Luther has stepped between Zlatko and you. Luther: “No… Not this time…” Zlatko: “I said get outta my way or I’ll shoot right through you… How dare you?!”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The garden
questions.situation: You are Connor. November 6, 7:51 PM. You emerge in the garden inside your programming where your handler Amanda meets you. Rain is falling; she stands under an umbrella. You: “Hello, Amanda.” Amanda: “Connor, I’ve been expecting you… Would you mind a little walk?” She is about to give her verdict on this afternoon’s hunt for a deviant.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Two failures?
questions.situation: You are Connor, walking with Amanda in the rain. The deviant you hunted this afternoon was not caught.

options.text: PRAGMATIC: agree that you may not be suited for this investigation, and suggest she replace you.
EXPLAIN: say deviants are irrational and hard to anticipate, but you should have been more effective.
NO EXCUSE: say you have no excuse; you should have been more efficient.

questions.title: What did you learn?
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the garden with Amanda. She wants to know what you learned about the deviant from this afternoon.

options.text: DIARY: tell her you found its diary, but it is encrypted.
SIGNS ON WALLS: describe the labyrinths and symbols that covered the walls of its apartment.
BIRDS: tell her it was fascinated by birds.

questions.title: What else?
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the garden with Amanda. Amanda: “What else?”

options.text: DIARY: tell her you found its diary, but it is encrypted.
SIGNS ON WALLS: describe the labyrinths and symbols that covered the walls of its apartment.
BIRDS: tell her it was fascinated by birds.

questions.title: The self-destruct
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the garden with Amanda. Amanda: “You came very close to capturing that deviant… It’s a pity you let it self-destruct…”

options.text: EXCUSE: say it was in Lieutenant Hank’s custody; you could not anticipate he would let it get away.
HESITATED: admit it claimed to be innocent and you were confused for a moment; it was a mistake.
LAST WORDS: admit your mistake, and repeat what it said before it jumped.
EXPLAIN: say deviants tend to self-destruct under stress, but you did not expect it to jump.

questions.title: The lieutenant
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the garden with Amanda. Amanda: “How is your relationship with the Lieutenant developing?”

options.text: SAVING HANK: say he seemed grateful that you saved his life on the roof.
CONNOR’S DEATH: say he finds it hard when a Connor is destroyed and replaced.
NEGATIVE: say he is openly hostile and shows no interest in the investigation.
AMBIGUOUS: say it is improving; you are coming to know him better.
POSITIVE: say it is improving; you have come to understand him better.

questions.title: Arrive at the lieutenant’s house
questions.situation: You are Connor. A taxi drops you outside Lieutenant Hank’s house. Taxi: “You have reached your destination. Thank you for travelling with Detroit Taxis. We look forward to seeing you again soon.” A homicide was reported 43 minutes ago; you could not find Hank at Jimmy’s bar, so you have come to see if he is at home. At the door you call: “Lieutenant Hank? Anybody home?” Nobody answers.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Find the lieutenant
questions.situation: You are Connor, outside Lieutenant Hank’s house. Nobody answers the door. There is a doorbell; a window to the left of the front door and one to the right; a car in the driveway; and round the corner on the right, the back living-room window and the kitchen window. You can do one thing at a time, in any order.

options.text: Knock on the front door.
Ring the doorbell.
Ring the doorbell again.
Check the car in the driveway: look in through its window.
Look in through the window to the left of the door (the bedroom).
Look in through the window to the right of the door (the front of the living room).
Go round the corner and look in through the back living-room window.
Look in through the kitchen window, and break in if you see something wrong.

questions.title: The dog
questions.situation: You are Connor, climbing in through the broken kitchen window. Hank lies on the floor. A big dog charges at you, snarling.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Analyze the lieutenant
questions.situation: You are Connor, kneeling beside Hank on the kitchen floor. He is unconscious. A whisky bottle and a revolver lie on the floor near him; his dog lies close by, watching you. You can scan one thing at a time, then wake him.

options.text: Scan his mouth.
Scan his chest.
Scan the whisky bottle.
Scan the revolver.
Look at the dog lying near him.
Wake him up.

questions.title: Take the lieutenant to the bathroom
questions.situation: You are Connor, shaking Hank awake: “Lieutenant? Wake up, Lieutenant! It’s me, Connor!”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Under the shower
questions.situation: You are Connor, in Hank’s bathroom. He sits soaked in the bathtub. Hank: “TURN IT OFF! TURN IT OFF! What the fuck are you doing here?” You: “A homicide was reported 43 minutes ago. I couldn’t find you at Jimmy’s bar, so I came to see if you were at home.” Hank: “Jesus, I must be the only cop in the world that gets assaulted in his own house by his own fuckin’ android… Can’t you just leave me alone?”

options.text: RATIONAL: say you cannot leave; you were programmed to investigate this case and cannot do it without him.
AGGRESSIVE: warn him that if he cannot conduct this investigation, you will have to inform his superiors.
SOLUTION: tell him he seems to have personal issues and should consult a professional.
PRAGMATIC: suggest he drop the case, so they assign someone else and you can focus on your mission.

questions.title: Beat it
questions.situation: You are Connor, in Hank’s bathroom. Hank: “Beat it! You hear me?! Get the hell outta here!”

options.text: TEASE: say it probably wasn’t interesting anyway: a man found dead in a sex club downtown.
LEAVE: say you understand and hope he comes to terms with his situation, and tell him what the case is.

questions.title: A shirt for the lieutenant
questions.situation: You are Connor, in Hank’s bedroom, fetching him clothes. You call: “What do you want to wear?” Hank: “Whatever.” There are three shirts to choose from: a hippy shirt, a streaky shirt and a stripy shirt.

options.text: Take the hippy shirt.
Take the streaky shirt.
Take the stripy shirt.

questions.title: The lieutenant’s magazines and television
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank has shut himself in the bathroom for five minutes. Two magazines lie on the floor of his bedroom, and the television in the living room is on.

options.text: Watch the evening news.
Read Century: “Time to Pull the Plug”.
Read Century: “Tainted Love”.
Take the time to go through all of it.
Move on without looking.

questions.title: Wait for the lieutenant
questions.situation: You are Connor, alone in Hank’s house while he gets dressed in the bathroom. His dog sleeps near the door. On the kitchen table there is a framed photograph; on the floor lies his revolver; on a table in the living room there is a record, and there is a picture above the fireplace by the TV. You can look at one thing at a time, or just wait for him.

options.text: Look at the photograph on the kitchen table.
Look at the record on the living-room table and the picture above the fireplace.
Pet the dog sleeping by the door.
Go to the bathroom door.
Look at the broken kitchen window.
Pick up the upturned kitchen chair.
Look at the revolver on the kitchen floor.
Wait for Hank.

questions.title: The revolver
questions.situation: You are Connor, holding Hank’s revolver, picked up from the kitchen floor: a .357 Magnum with 1 bullet remaining. Hank is in the bathroom.

options.text: QUESTION: ask Hank what he was doing with the gun.
SAY NOTHING: keep it to yourself.

questions.title: The lieutenant is ready
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank comes out of the bathroom, dressed, and stops by his dog: “Be a good dog, Sumo. I won’t be long.”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Hunting for parts
questions.situation: You are Markus. It is night, and rain is falling on the docks. Jericho is running out of everything; its androids are shutting down for lack of spare parts and blue blood, and you have come to steal some. You climb onto the dock with North, Simon and Josh. Josh: “This is crazy... If they catch us, we’re dead...” Simon: “What do we do now?” You: “We need to find the CyberLife warehouse. That’s where they keep the spare parts and the blue blood.” North: “Follow me!” You follow her between the rows of shipping containers while dock workers load cargo nearby. Simon: “Humans... Don’t let them see us...” Two guards are standing at the far end of a row. You edge toward them and are almost seen before you rejoin the group. North: “Watch out!” You climb onto the containers and make your way across them toward the CyberLife yard. Simon: “There are surveillance drones everywhere... We need to be careful...”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The crane
questions.situation: You are Markus, on top of the containers. Ahead, a crane is swinging a crate across the gap toward the warehouse. North and Josh have jumped onto it. North: “Markus, climb up here!” Simon has gone the other way and is jumping from container to container. The crate will not wait long.

options.text: Jump onto the crate on the crane with North and Josh.
Go around with Simon, jumping across the containers.

questions.title: The drone
questions.situation: You are Markus, crouched with the others at the edge of the CyberLife yard. A security drone hovers in front of the warehouse, blocking the way in. Simon: “CyberLife warehouses… They have everything we’re looking for…” North: “First, we have to get rid of that drone…” You: “Leave it to me.” You work out a climbing route up the stacked crates. From the top you could jump onto the drone and bring it down.

options.text: Climb up the crates and jump onto the drone to bring it down.

questions.title: Reach CyberLife
questions.situation: You are Markus. The drone is down. The four of you get into the CyberLife warehouse, a hall of stacked crates under harsh lights. You pry the first crate open and find biocomponents and blue blood. Simon: “Quick, open the other crates and fill your bags. Take as much as you can!”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The security android
questions.situation: You are Markus, bent over an open crate and filling your bag. A security android in a CyberLife uniform steps around the crates and stops in front of you: “You are trespassing on private property. Your presence constitutes a Level 2 infraction. I will notify security.” Before he can, a human guard calls from across the warehouse, coming closer: “John! John! Goddamn machine... where is it this time?” The others are crouched behind the crates. The guard has not seen any of you yet.

options.text: KILL GUARD: attack the human guard before he can raise the alarm.
GRAB AND HIDE: seize the security android and pull him into cover with you.
RUN AWAY: get everyone out before the guard arrives.
HIDE: stay hidden behind the crates and hope the guard walks past.

questions.title: The guard searches

They run on auto pilot, but they can be driven manually with a key.” You: “Where is this key?” John: “Down there, in the control station. There are two human guards. You’ll have to get the key without being noticed.” Simon: “This is suicide, Markus. Our bags are full. We got what we came for, let’s go before they catch us.” North: “This is a truck full of spare parts… There’d be enough for all of us… We can’t pass this up!” Josh: “And if we get killed, our people will have nothing. One guard: “Goddamn dogs… What the fuck are they barking at?..” The other: “Could be the weather… They don’t like storms…” “Yeah, I was going to take my kids camping this weekend. So much for that.” “Is Mike still in Zone 4?” “Looks like it… He should be done already…” “Better off in here than out patrolling in that.” Around you: a gun in a case on the wall, a screwdriver by the server cabinet, and, outside the window, a stack of oil drums.

questions.title: The Eden Club
questions.situation: You are Connor, the android investigator assigned to cases involving deviant androids, working with Lieutenant Hank. It is 8:17 pm. You have driven Hank’s car to the address in the report, a sex club called the Eden Club; Hank is badly hungover. “Aw… Feels like somebody’s playing with a drill inside my skull… You sure this is the place?” “It’s the address in the report.” “Right... Okay... Let’s get going.” Inside, club androids pose in lit display pods along the walls. “Jesus… Sexiest androids in town… Now I know why you insisted on coming here! Oh, boy…” Outside the room where the body was found, the club manager is pleading with an officer, Ben: “You’re not gonna take my license, are you? I mean, ha, I had nothing to do with this!” Ben: “The investigation’s ongoing, sir, I can’t tell you anything for the moment. Hey, Hank!” “Hey, Ben. How’s it goin’?” “It’s that room there. Oh, uh, by the way… Gavin’s in there too.” Hank: “Oh, great! A dead body and an asshole, just what I needed…” In the room, Detective Gavin and Officer Chris stand over a dead man on the bed; a damaged Traci, a WR400 club android, lies switched off on the floor. Gavin: “Lieutenant Anderson and his plastic pet… The fuck are you two doin’ here?” “We’ve been assigned all cases involving androids.” “Oh, yeah? Well, you’re wasting your time. Just some pervert who, uh, got more action than he could handle.” Hank: “We’ll have a look anyway, if you don’t mind.” Gavin: “Come on, let’s go… It’s, uh, starting to stink of booze in here…” Chris: “Night, Lieutenant.” They leave you the room.

questions.title: The Tracis attack
questions.situation: You are Connor. As you lean in over the pile, the two Tracis burst out of it. The brown-haired one throws herself at you; the blue-haired one goes for Hank. Hank: “DON’T MOVE!” The brown-haired Traci drives you back into the storage room, punching, kicking and grabbing whatever she can use as a weapon. Metal shelves of equipment stand to your left and to your right.

options.text: Knock over the shelf on your left onto her.
Pull down the shelf on your right onto her.
Do not fight back: let her go.

questions.title: The alley
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the fenced alley behind the warehouse. The brown-haired Traci is still on her feet and coming at you again; the blue-haired one is close behind her, beside a plastic chair and a row of trash cans.

options.text: Kick the chair into her.
Grab the blue-haired Traci and throw her into the other one.
Do not fight back: let them go.

questions.title: The two Tracis
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the alley behind the Eden Club’s warehouse, holding Hank’s gun. You won the fight. The brown-haired Traci picks herself up and runs straight at you, unarmed; the blue-haired one, the Traci who left the dead man’s room, is behind her. Hank is still getting up. You have a moment to decide.

options.text: SHOOT: fire at the brown-haired Traci as she runs at you.
SPARE: hold your fire.

questions.title: The two Tracis on the fence
questions.situation: You are Connor, down in the alley and badly damaged. You lost the fight. The two Tracis stop. The blue-haired one, the Traci who left the dead man’s room, looks down at you: “When that man broke the other Traci... I knew I was next… I was so scared… I begged him to stop, but he wouldn’t… And so I put my hands around his throat, and I squeezed... until he stopped moving… I didn’t mean to kill him… I just wanted to stay alive… get back to the one I love. I wanted her to hold me in her arms again... make me forget about the humans… their smell of sweat and their dirty words…” The brown-haired one: “Come on, let’s go.” They turn their backs on you and start up the fence. Hank’s gun lies within reach; you pick it up.

options.text: SHOOT: shoot them in the back as they climb.
SPARE: let them go.

questions.title: Highway to help
questions.situation: You are Kara. It is one in the morning on November 7th, and snow is falling hard. You are on the road in Zlatko’s car with Alice and Luther, the big android who turned against Zlatko and helped you escape his house. You are heading for the people Luther says help androids cross the border.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: In the car
questions.situation: You are Kara, in Zlatko’s car, driving through the snow at night. Luther sits to your left; Alice is on the back seat. The board computer on the dashboard has a TV screen. You can do one thing at a time, or simply let the drive go on.

options.text: Switch on the TV on the dashboard and watch the news.
Change the channel once more.
CAR: say it is a good thing Zlatko had a car.
DESTINATION: ask Luther how he knows about the people you are going to see.
DISTANCE: ask whether it is much farther.
WEATHER: say you have never seen snow before.
Turn around and look at Alice on the back seat.
Let the drive go on.

questions.title: The car breaks down
questions.situation: You are Kara. The car’s voice: “Malfunction detected. Emergency brakes activated.” The car stops on the empty road in the snow. Luther: “This doesn’t look good.” You: “Stay inside, Alice.” You get out and open the hood: the car will not go any further. “What are we going to do?” Luther: “I don’t know… Continue on foot, I guess… There’s nowhere we can stay around here, Kara…” You: “It’s 30°, Alice won’t make it!.. We have to find somewhere to spend the night.” Up the road stands a big sign for an amusement park, Pirates’ Cove.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Inside Pirates’ Cove
questions.situation: You are Kara. With Alice and Luther you walk in through the gates of Pirates’ Cove, a pirate-themed amusement park lying under the snow. You: “We need to find shelter. We have to get out of the cold.” Luther: “Looks like it’s been abandoned for a while…”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The fun fair
questions.situation: You are Kara, in the snow inside the abandoned park with Alice and Luther, looking for somewhere to spend the night. By the entrance, on your left, is a map of the park covered in snow. Small buildings line the road. A little way in, on the right, an android stands frozen in the ice, and in the middle of the road is a fortune-teller android in a glass box. The road leads on toward a Ferris wheel. You can look around, one thing at a time, or go on to the end of the road.

options.text: Check one of the buildings along the road.
Examine the android frozen in the ice.
Switch on the fortune-teller android in the glass box.
Wipe the snow off the park map and look at it.
Go on to the end of the road, toward the Ferris wheel.

questions.title: The tavern
questions.situation: You are Kara, outside the boarded-up tavern. Luther rips the planks off and breaks the door in: “I’ll handle this. There we go.” Inside it is dark and cold: an old pirate tavern, abandoned like the rest of the park. You put your flashlight down on some barrels by the entrance. You: “I don’t think we’ll find anything better… Let’s settle in for the night.” Luther: “I’ll get a fire going.”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The magazine on the barrels
questions.situation: You are Kara, inside the tavern. On the barrels where you put down your flashlight lies a magazine with two covers.

options.text: Read Detroit Today: USS Iowa Missing.
Read Gossips Weekly: All-Android Band Tipped for Music Prize.
Take the time to go through all of it.
Move on without looking.

questions.title: Luther starts a fire
questions.situation: You are Kara, in the tavern. Luther builds a fire on the floor in the middle of the room: “I’ll make the fire here, that way we won’t be smoked out…”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The tavern
questions.situation: You are Kara, in the abandoned tavern with Alice and Luther. On a wall by the windows someone has written something in red, and there is a leaflet on the floor beneath it. By the door are a window and a one-legged pirate. What you must do is make Alice a bed for the night: there are curtains on the windows and a pirate pillow. You can look around first, one thing at a time.

options.text: Look at the red writing on the wall.
Look at the leaflet on the floor.
Look through the window by the door.
Look at the one-legged pirate by the door.
Make a bed for Alice: tear the curtain off the second window and fetch the pirate pillow.

questions.title: The poster
questions.situation: You are Kara. You find Alice standing in front of a big old poster of a happy family, looking up at it. Without turning round she asks: “Do you think we’ll be like them some day?..”

options.text: OPTIMISTIC: say that once you cross the border you can start over, and be like them.
REALISTIC: say you will never be like them, but you can be happy in your own way.
SINCERE: say you do not know how to be like them, but maybe you can be your own family.

questions.title: The bag
questions.situation: You are Kara. Alice is lying in the bed you made, still awake. Next to her bed is the bag you brought with you. You can open it before you go and sit with her.

options.text: OFFER COOKIE: offer Alice the cookies left in the bag.
Look at the gun in the bag.
Go and sit with Alice.

questions.title: Goodnight
questions.situation: You are Kara, sitting by Alice’s bed in the tavern. She is lying under the curtain you tore down, looking up at you. What do you say to her?

options.text: REASSURE: tell her Luther and you will be right here.
CONSOLE: say it has been another tough day, and things will look better in the morning.
KISS: kiss her goodnight.
TOMORROW: tell her to get some rest, because tomorrow is going to be a long day.

questions.title: A story
questions.situation: You are Kara, telling Alice a story by her bed.

options.text: PRINCESS: begin a story about a princess.
UNICORN: begin a story about a unicorn.
KNIGHT: begin a story about a knight.
UNHAPPY: a little girl who was not very happy.
FEAR: a little girl who was tired of being afraid.
ALONE: a little girl who lived alone in a big old house.
IMPOSSIBLE: deep down, she knew she could not.
SHADOW: the shadow that lived within her kept her from being happy.
DIFFERENT: she was different, and that made her very sad.
UNHAPPY: a robot who was not very happy either.
OBEDIENT: a robot programmed to obey, who felt for once that she should disobey.
LOST: a robot just as lost as the little girl.
BETTER LIFE: to try to find a better life.
SHADOW: to escape the shadow that haunted that house.
LIVE IN PEACE: to find a place where they could be safe.
BRAVE: they were so brave that they escaped them all.
TOGETHER: they stuck together, so they overcame them all.
FREE: they wanted so badly to be free that they overcame them all.
GIANT: a gentle giant who promised to protect them.
GUARDIAN: another robot who left his master to become their guardian.
ROBOT: another robot who left his master to travel with them.
REALISTIC: say it is up to the two of you to write the end of the story.
MORAL: say you do not know, but when you reach the end you will know what it meant.
HAPPY END: say they reach the place they dream of and live happily ever after.

questions.title: Talking to Luther
questions.situation: You are Kara. Alice is asleep. You sit down with Luther by the window. Luther: “She’s a sweet girl…” You: “Yes, she’s very brave…” What do you talk about?

options.text: rA9: ask him whether he has ever heard of rA9.
rA9 DOUBTS: ask what if rA9 is just a story you tell each other to keep going.
SNOW: remark that it is still snowing.
PLANS: ask what he is going to do when you reach Canada.
LUTHER’S PAST: ask whether he remembers anything from his life before Zlatko.
Say nothing more.

questions.title: Luther’s question
questions.situation: You are Kara, by the window with Luther. He hesitates: “Kara, have you ever... Noticed anything? About Alice?..”

options.text: YES: say of course, she is a wonderful little girl, really special.
WHAT?: ask him what he means.
NO: ask him what he is talking about.

questions.title: Shadows attack
questions.situation: You are Kara. Alice has screamed your name. Figures have broken into the tavern and are coming at you out of the dark: a whole group of them, closing in on Alice, Luther and you. The fire is burning in the middle of the room.

options.text: GRAB GUN: grab the gun from your bag.
GRAB BURNING STICK: snatch a burning stick from the fire.
PROTECT ALICE: put yourself between Alice and them.
PUT OUT FIRE: put out the fire.

questions.title: The figures close in
questions.situation: You are Kara. The figures keep coming toward you out of the dark.

options.text: SHOOT IN THE AIR: fire a warning shot.
QUESTION: demand to know who they are and what they want.
PUSH BACK: drive them back.

questions.title: The Jerrys
questions.situation: You are Kara. The figures stop. In the light they are all the same android, a crowd of them. One of them speaks: “Don’t be afraid! We don’t wanna hurt you. We’re just like you… Our name is Jerry. We were working here before the park closed… We didn’t mean to frighten you, but sometimes humans come to hurt us, so we wanted to see who was there… What are you doing here?” You: “We were looking for shelter for the night… We’ll be gone tomorrow. The…” Jerry: “A little girl!.. We haven’t seen one for a long time… Children used to love to come and see us. She looks sad… We have something to show her! Something fun! She’ll love it!.. Does she want to see?” You: “The last few days have been difficult…” Jerry: “We have something to show her! Something fun! She’ll love it!.. Does she want to see?” You: “Oh, I don’t think she’s…” Jerry: “She should follow us then!” You: “Alice, I don’t know if it’s a good idea!..” Luther: “I don’t think you have any choice…” Alice: “Come on, Kara!”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: The carousel
questions.situation: You are Kara. The Jerrys lead you through the snow to the old carousel: “Be our guest!” You switch it on, and it still works. Jerry: “The little one can climb on board. The carousel is about to begin!” You lift Alice onto the ride.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: A quiet moment
questions.situation: You are Kara, watching Alice ride the carousel on a seahorse while the Jerrys look on, some of them hopping in place with excitement. You: “It’s the first time I’ve seen her smile…” Luther: “She hasn’t had much to smile about lately.”

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Ambassador Bridge
questions.situation: You are Connor. It is 1:19 in the morning on November 7, a few hours after the club. Hank has driven the two of you to a snowy park on the riverbank and stopped by the path; across the dark river the lit bridge to Canada spans the water. He gets out without a word, walks to a bench facing the river and sits down with a drink. You get out of the car.

options.text: Continue.

questions.title: Two magazines on the park bench
questions.situation: You are Connor, standing by the car on the snowy path. Hank sits on a bench by the river with his back to you. On the bench straight ahead of you lie two magazines.

options.text: Read Century: The Mysterious Mister Kamski.
Read Detroit Today: Markets Predict War.
Take the time to go through all of it.
Move on without looking.

questions.title: Hank on the bench
questions.situation: You are Connor. You walk over to the bench where Hank sits drinking, looking across the river at the lit bridge. Hank: “Nice view, huh?... I used to come here a lot before…” What do you say?

options.text: PERSONAL QUESTION: ask whether you can ask him a personal question.
STOP DRINKING: tell him he should stop drinking, for the sake of his health.
BEFORE: ask what he meant by “before”.
GO BACK: say it is late and he should go home.

questions.title: A personal question
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank has grudgingly let you ask him something personal. You remember the photograph of a child on his kitchen table, and the revolver on the floor beside him. What do you ask?

options.text: PHOTO: ask about the photo of a child on his kitchen table.
SUICIDE: ask why he is so determined to kill himself.

questions.title: The investigation
questions.situation: You are Connor, still beside Hank on the bench. You bring up the case: “We’re not making any progress on this investigation… The deviants have nothing in common. They’re all different models, produced at different times, in different places…” Hank: “Well, there must be some link.” What do you suggest?

options.text: rA9: say what they have in common is an obsession with rA9, a kind of myth.
SHOCK: say the deviants all went through an emotional shock, a trauma or a sense of injustice.
SYSTEMS: suggest a hardware problem, perhaps a defective biocomponent.
SOFTWARE: suggest a software problem that only occurs under certain conditions.

questions.title: The two girls at the club
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank stares at the water. You ask: “You seem preoccupied, Lieutenant… Is it something to do with what happened back at the Eden Club?” Hank: “Those two girls… They just wanted to be together… They really seemed in love…” What do you answer?

options.text: RATIONAL: say they can simulate human emotions, but machines feel nothing.
DEVIANTS: say they did not want anything; they were deviants, end of story.
IRONIC: remark that you did not think machines could affect him like this.
COLD: say nothing in their program allows them to love or desire anything.

questions.title: The girl you never found
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank stares at the water. You ask: “You seem preoccupied, Lieutenant… Is it something to do with what happened back at the Eden Club?” Hank: “I wish we’d have found that girl that killed that guy… Maybe she had a reason… Maybe she was just defending herself…” What do you answer?

options.text: COLD: ask what difference it would make; a defective machine killed a human.
IRONIC: remark that you did not think machines could affect him like this.
RATIONAL: say it did not want anything; it was a deviant, nothing more.

questions.title: What are you really?
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank turns to look at you. “What about you, Connor?... You look human, you sound human, but what are you really?”

options.text: COLD: say you are a machine, designed to accomplish a task.
AGGRESSIVE: say you are a machine with a reason to live, unlike him.
DEFENSIVE: say he knows exactly what you are, and it has nothing to do with the investigation.
NEUTRAL: say you are whatever he wants you to be: partner, drinking buddy, or just a machine.

questions.title: Why didn’t you shoot?
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank: “You could’ve shot those two girls, but you didn’t. Why didn’t you shoot, Connor? Hm? Some scruples suddenly enter into your program?”

options.text: LIE: say you would have shot them if you could.
TRUTH: admit you simply decided not to shoot.

questions.title: Did you feel anything?
questions.situation: You are Connor. Hank: “Did you feel anything when you shot those two girls, fucking bastard? Or were you just executing some program?”

options.text: COLD: say you only neutralized two machines and never hesitated.
DEFENSIVE: say this is going nowhere and you will go back to the station.
AGGRESSIVE: mock his sudden interest in machines.
